deck.title: The Other Databases (keyword zoo)
deck.analogy: A hardware store wall of fifty screwdrivers: each AWS specialty database exists for one screw head, and the exam hands you the screw (keyword in, service out).

subtopics.title: The two comparisons worth 30 extra seconds

cards.front: What is the exam approach to AWS specialty databases (Redshift, Neptune, QLDB, etc.)?

back.answer: Each engine has ONE identifying keyword; match the keyword in the question to the service.
back.explanation: You don't need to master them; the question hands you the screw head.
back.mnemonic: Hardware store wall of screwdrivers: glance at the screw, grab the right handle.

cards.front: OLTP vs OLAP: what workload does each describe?

back.answer: OLTP: many small operations touching few rows. OLAP: few huge scans over billions of rows.
back.explanation: OLTP examples: fetch order #123. OLAP example: average revenue per region per month across five years.

cards.front: Which AWS databases are OLTP, and what storage style do they use?

back.answer: RDS, Aurora, DynamoDB are OLTP app databases; row-based storage grabs the whole record at once.

cards.front: Why is columnar storage used by OLAP warehouses like Redshift?

back.answer: Data is stored column-by-column, so scanning one column doesn't read other fields; it also compresses well.
back.explanation: Analytics reads billions of rows but only a few columns, so columnar is massively faster.

cards.front: Analysts run big reporting queries on the production database and the app slows. What's the fix?

back.answer: Never run analytics on prod OLTP; move analytics to Redshift (or a Read Replica/Athena per scenario).
back.explanation: This is the cardinal sin: mixing OLAP scans with OLTP workloads.

cards.front: Redshift: what is it and what keywords identify it?

back.answer: A data warehouse: OLAP, BI, analytics, petabyte-scale, columnar.
back.explanation: Load data in, then point Tableau/QuickSight at it.

cards.front: What is Redshift Spectrum?

back.answer: Querying data still in S3 from Redshift without loading it.

cards.front: What is Redshift Serverless?

back.answer: The same Redshift warehouse with no cluster to manage, pay per use.

cards.front: Athena: what is it and how is it priced?

back.answer: Serverless SQL directly on files in S3; $5 per TB scanned.
back.explanation: Keyword: analyze logs in S3 with SQL, no infrastructure.

cards.front: Neptune: what type of database and which use cases?

back.answer: Graph database for relationship-heavy data: social networks, recommendations, fraud rings, knowledge graphs.

cards.front: QLDB: what is its identifying feature?

back.answer: A centralized ledger with immutable, cryptographically verifiable history; nothing can be changed or deleted.
back.explanation: You can prove the history is intact.

cards.front: QLDB vs Managed Blockchain?

back.answer: QLDB is centralized (one owner); Managed Blockchain is decentralized for multiple untrusting parties with no central authority.

cards.front: Timestream: what is it for?

back.answer: Time-series database for IoT sensor data, telemetry, and DevOps metrics queried by time window.

cards.front: DocumentDB: what is the identifying keyword?
Keyspaces: what is the identifying keyword?
OpenSearch: what is it used for?

back.answer: Full-text/fuzzy search plus log analytics with dashboards (the old Elasticsearch/Kibana).
back.explanation: Searching "runing shoes" still finds running shoes.

cards.front: Athena vs Redshift vs Spectrum: when to use each?

back.answer: Athena: data stays in S3, ad-hoc, zero infra. Redshift: loaded warehouse, heavy repeated BI. Spectrum: query S3 from existing Redshift.

cards.sourceHeading: The two comparisons worth 30 extra seconds

cards.front: How do you reduce Athena query costs and improve performance?

back.answer: Use columnar formats (Parquet/ORC), compress the data, and partition it.
back.explanation: Athena bills per TB scanned, so all three shrink bytes scanned.

cards.sourceHeading: The two comparisons worth 30 extra seconds

cards.front: Why does partitioning reduce Athena cost?

back.answer: Queries skip irrelevant folders (e.g., by date), so fewer bytes are scanned.

cards.front: How do you add fuzzy/full-text search to DynamoDB data?

back.answer: DynamoDB + Streams → Lambda → OpenSearch; search queries go to OpenSearch.
back.explanation: DynamoDB can't do fuzzy or full-text search.
back.mnemonic: DynamoDB is a coat-check, not a librarian.

cards.front: A BI team needs a petabyte-scale data warehouse for complex analytical queries. Which service?

choices.why: OLTP row store, not petabyte analytics.

cards.front: Query data in S3 from an existing Redshift cluster without loading it. Which?

choices.why: Separate service, not from the Redshift cluster.
Doesn't address querying S3 in place.
Queries S3 data from Redshift unloaded.

cards.front: Run occasional SQL queries on ALB/VPC logs stored in S3 with minimal setup. Which?

choices.why: Serverless SQL directly on S3 files.

cards.front: How do you reduce Athena costs and speed up queries?

back.explanation: Bill is TB scanned, so scan less.

cards.front: A social app needs friend-of-friend recommendations and fraud ring detection. Which?
Complete, immutable, cryptographically verifiable financial history for a single organization. Which?
Multiple companies transact without a trusted central authority. Which?
Millions of IoT sensor readings per minute analyzed over time windows. Which?

choices.why: Ad-hoc SQL on S3, not time-series.

cards.front: Migrate a MongoDB workload to a managed AWS service. Which?
Migrate a Cassandra workload to a managed AWS service. Which?
A product catalog in DynamoDB needs fuzzy, typo-tolerant full-text search. Which?

choices.why: SQL on S3, not fuzzy search.

choices.text: OpenSearch fed by Streams and Lambda

cards.front: Analysts' reports are slowing the production OLTP database. What now?

back.answer: Move analytics off prod, to Redshift
